title: The Gathering of God’s People
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The gathering of God’s people is Christ’s promised gathering of His redeemed into His presence, safety, victory, and everlasting fellowship. The scattered people of God will be brought together with Him forever.
summary: The gathering of God’s people is Christ’s promised gathering of His redeemed into His presence, safety, victory, and everlasting fellowship. The scattered people of God will be brought together with Him forever.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gathers His sheep, calls His people to Himself, and will bring them safely into His presence. The One who saves His people will not lose them.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture promises that Christ will gather His people. No believer will be forgotten, lost, overlooked, or left outside His saving purpose.

This gathering includes victory and comfort. The dead in Christ will rise, living believers will be with the Lord, and God’s redeemed people will stand before Him.

The gathering of God’s people also shows the worldwide scope of salvation. Revelation pictures a multitude from every nation, tribe, people, and language before the throne and the Lamb.

This doctrine gives hope to the scattered, lonely, persecuted, displaced, and grieving. Christ knows His own and will bring them home.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers feel isolated, forgotten, or separated by suffering, death, persecution, disability, or rejection. The promise of gathering says Christ will gather every one of His people.

This doctrine also strengthens the church’s mission. The Lamb is worthy to gather worshipers from all peoples, and the Gospel goes out with that final gathering in view.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Take comfort that Christ will gather His people. Do not live as though loneliness, scattering, or death has the final word. Encourage the isolated, participate in the mission of the church, and wait for the day when all God’s people are with the Lord.
